lessons.title: Cheat sheet of every shortcut
lessons.why: Type a word to filter. Start here when stuck.

lessons.title: Drag any window
lessons.why: Hold Super, drag with the left mouse button.
lessons.more:
Hold Super, press the left mouse button anywhere inside a window (no title bar needed) and drag.

A tiled window lifts out of its spot; let go over another window and the tiles rearrange around it. A floating window moves wherever you drop it.

Try it now: hold Super and drag one window onto the side of another.

lessons.title: Resize with the mouse
lessons.why: Hold Super, drag with the right mouse button.
lessons.more:
Hold Super and drag with the right mouse button inside a window to resize it.

On tiled windows it moves the border between them: the neighbors shrink or grow to match, so you can give the window you're working in more room without touching the keyboard.

On a floating window it resizes the window itself, from the corner nearest your pointer.

Try both: resize two tiled windows, then float one with {float} and resize it.

lessons.title: Flip through desktops
lessons.why: Hold Super and roll the scroll wheel.
lessons.more:
Hold Super and roll the scroll wheel to step through your desktops, one notch at a time. It skips empty desktops, so you only land where you have windows.

Handy when your hand is already on the mouse. Add Alt (Super + Alt + scroll) to flip through the tabs of a group instead.

lessons.title: Launch any app
lessons.why: Type the app's name and press Enter.

lessons.title: Close the window you're in
lessons.why: Works on every app, the same way.

lessons.title: Jump between windows
lessons.why: Moves to the window in that direction.

lessons.title: Go to desktop 1 to 9
lessons.why: Each desktop is one number away.
lessons.more:
Omarchy calls them workspaces; think of them as separate desktops, each with its own windows. {workspace-switch} jumps straight to one (0 is the tenth).

A common setup is one desktop per kind of work, like email on 1, browser on 2 and terminals on 3. Then every app is always one key away.

lessons.title: Send a window to another desktop
lessons.why: You go along with it.
lessons.more:
Sends the window you're in to another desktop and takes you along with it.

To send it away and stay where you are, use {move-silent}.

lessons.title: True full screen
lessons.why: Covers everything, bar included.
lessons.more:
Covers the whole screen, bar included. Press {fullscreen} again to leave.

There's also tiled full screen, Super + Ctrl + F: the app acts as if it were full screen (a video player hides its controls, for example) while the window stays in its tile.

lessons.title: Screenshot
lessons.why: Pick an area, a window or the whole screen.

lessons.title: Clipboard history
lessons.why: Everything you've copied lately.
lessons.more:
Omarchy keeps a history of what you copy. {clipboard} opens it; pick an entry to paste it.

Related: Super + C and Super + V copy and paste the same way in every app, terminals included, where Ctrl + C would stop a running program.

lessons.title: Cycle through windows
lessons.why: Walks through the windows on this desktop.

lessons.title: Back to the last desktop
lessons.why: Like Alt + Tab, for desktops.

lessons.title: Float a window
lessons.why: Lifts it out of the tiles, on this desktop.
lessons.more:
Normally Omarchy tiles windows: they share the desktop automatically, with no overlap. A floating window sits on top instead, at its own size and position.

Drag it with {mouse-move} and resize it with {mouse-resize}. It stays on its own desktop. Press {float} again to tile it.

To float a window and keep it with you on every desktop, use pop-out ({pop-out}).

lessons.title: Swap a window with its neighbor
lessons.why: Rearrange tiles without the mouse.

lessons.title: Make a window full width
lessons.why: The whole desktop, bar kept. Again to undo.
lessons.more:
The window fills the desktop but keeps the bar and the gaps. Other windows on the desktop are still there underneath; press {full-width} again to bring them back.

Full screen ({fullscreen}) also covers the bar.

lessons.title: Emoji picker
lessons.why: Search and insert an emoji anywhere.

lessons.title: Dismiss a notification
lessons.why: Add Shift to clear them all.

lessons.title: Lock the screen
lessons.why: Before you walk away.

lessons.title: Show or hide the scratchpad
lessons.why: A hidden drawer over any desktop.
lessons.more:
Think of the scratchpad as a drawer that slides out over whatever desktop you're on. Windows in it keep running while hidden.

1. Put a window in with {scratchpad-move}. It disappears from its desktop.
2. Press {scratchpad} to pull the drawer out over the desktop you're on. Press it again to tuck it away.
3. To take a window out for good, open the drawer, click the window, and press {workspace-move}.

Good for things you check often but don't want taking up a tile: a chat app, music, a notes terminal.

lessons.title: Put a window in the scratchpad
lessons.why: Take it out with Super + Shift + number.
lessons.more:
Puts the window you're in into the scratchpad, a hidden drawer you pull out over any desktop with {scratchpad}.

To take it out again, open the drawer, click the window, and press {workspace-move}.

lessons.title: Pop out and pin a window
lessons.why: Floats on top and follows you everywhere.
lessons.more:
Pop-out floats the window, centers it at a comfortable size, and pins it, so it stays visible when you switch desktops. Press {pop-out} again to put it back in the tiles.

Float ({float}) only floats it, on its own desktop.

Pop-out suits a video call or a video you want to keep watching while you move between desktops.

lessons.title: Stack windows as tabs
lessons.why: Windows share one tile, like browser tabs.
lessons.more:
A group stacks several windows into one tile, with tabs on top, like a browser.

1. Press {group} on a window to make its tile a group.
2. Move a neighboring window in with Super + Alt + the arrow pointing toward the group.
3. Switch tabs with {group-next}, or click a tab. {group-out} takes a window back out.

Use it when you want several windows on one desktop but only need to see one at a time.

lessons.title: Next tab in a group
lessons.why: Flip through the windows in a group.
lessons.more:
Moves to the next window in a group, the way Ctrl + Tab moves between browser tabs. Add Shift to go back.

A group is several windows stacked in one tile with tabs on top; {group} makes one.

lessons.action: Move active window out of group
lessons.title: Pull a window out of a group
lessons.why: It goes back to being its own tile.
lessons.more: Takes the window you're in out of its group so it becomes its own tile again. The rest of the group stays together.

lessons.title: Flip side-by-side to stacked
lessons.why: Switches how two tiles share the space.
lessons.more:
In Omarchy's default layout, two windows sharing space sit side by side or one above the other. {split} flips the window you're in between the two.

It's the quickest fix when a window is too narrow to read.

lessons.title: Resize a tile
lessons.why: Shift: height. Alt: a little. Ctrl: a lot.
lessons.more:
Super + Minus and Super + Equal change the width of the window you're in. Add Shift to change the height, Alt to move a little, and Ctrl to move a lot.

With the mouse, use {mouse-resize}.

lessons.title: Send a window away and stay put
lessons.why: Like Super + Shift + number, but you stay.
lessons.more:
Like {workspace-move}, but you stay on the desktop you're on and the window goes on without you.

Handy for clearing your desk: push a finished terminal to desktop 9 to deal with later.

lessons.title: Copy text from anywhere on screen
lessons.why: Drag a box around text in any image or PDF.
lessons.more:
Drag a box around any text on screen: an image, a video frame, a PDF that won't let you select text. The text is read on your own computer (with Tesseract, no internet) and copied to your clipboard.

It works best on clear, decent-sized text.

lessons.title: Record the screen
lessons.why: Same picker as a screenshot, but video.

lessons.title: Grab any color on screen
lessons.why: Click a pixel; its hex code is copied.

lessons.title: Share menu
lessons.why: Send the clipboard or a file to a device.

lessons.title: Calculator
lessons.why: A quick calculator on top of everything.

lessons.title: Set a reminder
lessons.why: A desktop notification in a few minutes.

lessons.title: Do not disturb
lessons.why: Silence notifications for a meeting.

lessons.title: Notifications you missed
lessons.why: Everything that popped up while you were away.

lessons.title: Hide or show the top bar
lessons.why: A little more room for a presentation.

lessons.title: Switch themes
lessons.why: A new look for the whole desktop.

lessons.title: Change the wallpaper
lessons.why: Pick from the current theme's wallpapers.

lessons.title: System menu
lessons.why: Lock, suspend, restart or shut down.

lessons.title: Make a window solid
lessons.why: Turns off transparency for this window.

lessons.title: Turn window gaps off and on
lessons.why: Squeeze out every pixel on this desktop.

lessons.title: Switch this desktop's layout
lessons.why: Toggles between tiling layouts.
lessons.more:
Switches this desktop between Omarchy's two tiling layouts.

Dwindle, the default, splits the space in half for each new window. Scrolling lines windows up in columns side by side and you scroll along them, which suits a very wide screen.

The choice is per desktop and is remembered.

lessons.title: Pseudo-tile a window
lessons.why: Keeps its own size inside its tile.
lessons.more: In Omarchy's default layout, a pseudo-tiled window keeps its own preferred size and sits centered in its tile, instead of stretching to fill it. Useful for small dialogs or apps that look wrong stretched. Press again to undo.
